relevance_rank_note: Tests the B2 half of H4 directly and quantitatively, that apoE4 recycles out of endosomes far less than apoE3 in a human cell line, but measures no apoE-receptor binding and identifies no receptor; its Discussion attributes the apoE4 effect to low-pH conformational change and membrane association rather than receptor adhesion, so every row is a B surrogate.

description: In pulse-chase Western blots of the chase medium, HDL3 stimulated re-secretion of internalized TRL-derived apoE3 about 6-fold but apoE4 only 3.6-fold, so apoE4 recycles out of the endosomal compartment much less than apoE3.
quote: As determined by densitometric analysis of lanes 3–6, the HDL3-induced recycling of apoE3 was stimulated ∼6-fold, whereas apoE4 re-secretion was increased only 3.6-fold.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less HDL3-induced recycling of internalized apoE out of endosomes)
system: HuH7 human hepatoma cell line, triglyceride-rich lipoproteins from apoCII-deficient patients enriched with 5 ug/ml recombinant apoE3 or apoE4, 60 min pulse at 37 C then heparin wash and 60 min chase with or without 50 ug/ml HDL3, recycled apoE in the chase medium detected by anti-apoE Western blot and quantified by densitometry, three independent experiments
human_check: No figure image was viewed; the densitometry values 6-fold and 3.6-fold are printed in the Results text and the legend. Effect recorded as the apoE3 stimulation 6x with the apoE4 stimulation 3.6x in the description, because the authors print the two fold-stimulations separately and never print a single apoE3-versus-apoE4 ratio; computing one would be a read-off. Effect detail: apoE3 ~6-fold HDL3 stimulation vs apoE4 3.6-fold. No P value is stated for the apoE3-versus-apoE4 contrast in the text or legend.

description: In radiolabelled pulse-chase experiments, HDL3-induced re-secretion of TRL-derived apoE3 was about 2-fold higher than apoE4 at both 60 and 240 min of chase, independently confirming reduced apoE4 recycling.
quote: In this set of experiments, HDL3-induced recycling of TRL-derived 125I-apoE3 was increased ∼2-fold at t = 60 and 240 min compared with 125I-apoE4.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (about half as much apoE re-secreted during chase)
system: HuH7 human hepatoma cell line pre-loaded 60 min at 37 C with 125I-apoE3-TRL or 125I-apoE4-TRL, heparin wash, chase 60 or 240 min at 37 C with or without 50 ug/ml HDL3, re-secreted 125I-apoE in the medium counted and normalised to cell protein, four independent experiments with triplicate samples
human_check: No figure image was viewed. The ~2-fold is printed in the Results text as apoE3 over apoE4 and holds at both chase times; the legend gives no P value and no star key for this panel, so P is not_found_in_source rather than ambiguous_panel. n = 4 independent experiments with triplicate samples.

description: Cell-surface binding of 125I-labelled apoE4-VLDL at 4 C was 1.5-1.8-fold higher than apoE3-VLDL on human hepatoma cells, a tighter cell-surface association of apoE4, though no receptor was identified or measured.
quote: In these experiments, cell-surface binding and internalization of 125I-apoE4-VLDL was increased 1.5–1.8-fold compared with 125I-apoE3-VLDL.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more apoE-lipoprotein bound at the cell surface at 4 C)
system: HuH7 human hepatoma cell line incubated 60 min at 4 C with 2.5-10 ug/ml 125I-VLDL from patients homozygous for apoE3 or for apoE4, washed, lysed in 0.1 N NaOH and specific bound radioactivity counted per mg cell protein, three independent experiments with triplicate samples
human_check: CLASS CALL: recorded as class 3, not class 1. The assay is bulk 4 C binding of whole VLDL particles to intact cells; no ApoE-receptor binding is measured and no receptor is identified, and the Discussion attributes the apoE4 difference to its greater propensity to form a molten globule at low pH and to increased association with endosomal membranes rather than to receptor adhesion, so this is a B1 surrogate rather than a measured apoE-receptor interaction. No figure image was viewed. The legend gives a star key, '**, p < 0.01; ***, p < 0.001 by Student's t test', shared by panels C and D and does not say which panel or which bar carries which star, and the text states no P for this contrast, so P is N/A + ambiguous_panel. Effect: the text prints a 1.5-1.8-fold range spanning binding (C) and uptake (D) together; the top of the range is recorded and the range is in the description. Effect detail: 1.5-1.8-fold increase, printed jointly for surface binding and internalisation.

description: Internalisation of 125I-apoE4-VLDL at 37 C was 1.5-1.8-fold higher than apoE3-VLDL, so more apoE4 accumulated inside the human hepatoma cells.
quote: Using radiolabeled VLDL from patients homozygous for apoE3 or apoE4, similar results were obtained in radioactive cell-surface binding (Fig. 2C) and uptake experiments (Fig. 2D), respectively.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more apoE internalised and retained intracellularly)
system: HuH7 human hepatoma cell line incubated 60 min at 37 C with 2.5-10 ug/ml 125I-VLDL from patients homozygous for apoE3 or for apoE4, surface material removed by washing, cells lysed and internalised radioactivity counted per mg cell protein, three independent experiments with triplicate samples
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Separate row from Fig 2C because 4 C surface binding and 37 C internalisation are two panels and two different measurements, although the authors print one shared 1.5-1.8-fold range for both; the top of the range is recorded and the range is in the description. Effect detail: 1.5-1.8-fold increase, printed jointly for surface binding and internalisation. Legend star key '**, p < 0.01; ***, p < 0.001' is shared between panels C and D with no panel or bar assignment, so P is N/A + ambiguous_panel. Intracellular accumulation of apoE alone is a weak surrogate for receptor adhesion, hence strength 4.

description: Degradation of internalized TRL-derived apoE was similar for apoE3 and apoE4 over a 30-300 min chase, with most apoprotein escaping proteolysis, so differential degradation does not explain the apoE4 accumulation; a null on this readout.
quote: Consistent with the results described above, most of the radiolabeled apoproteins escaped proteolytic degradation and only some degradation products (up to 25% after 300 min), probably derived from apoB, appeared in the media.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in intracellular degradation of internalized apoE)
system: HuH7 human hepatoma cell line incubated 60 min at 37 C with 10 ug/ml 125I-apoE3-VLDL or 125I-apoE4-VLDL, 4 C wash and heparin release of cell-bound material, second incubation 30-300 min at 37 C, trichloroacetic acid-soluble 125I-tyrosine in the medium measured as a percentage of total metabolized radioactivity, four separate experiments with triplicate samples
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Marked against: true as a null, following the convention that nulls and non-significant results carry that flag; it is a null on degradation, which is not itself a B readout for H4 but is the authors' control excluding differential degradation as the cause of apoE4 accumulation. The text states the similarity qualitatively ('the relative amount of degraded apoproteins was similar between the isoforms', Discussion) and prints no isoform-resolved percentages or P value for the apoE3-versus-apoE4 contrast, so eff is qualitative and P is not_found_in_source. Relevance kept low because degradation is one step removed from receptor adhesion or recycling.
